Evidence_Result: 12 mg/day astaxanthin for four weeks produced no statistically or clinically significant cardiometabolic or fire-ground performance effect; most inflammatory changes were within treatment groups.
Sixteen studies reported inconsistent and mostly modest performance/recovery findings; authors state there is inadequate practical evidence for field performance guidance.

Creatine group showed larger improvement in rescue (difference 1.78 s, 95% CI 0.61-2.95; p=.004) and forcible entry (2.66 s, 95% CI 0.68-4.65; p=.01), with no interaction for other tasks or total time.
End-running speed, maximal heart rate and predicted VO2max test-retest ICCs were .971, .960 and .975; authors report validity/usefulness against treadmill and 2-mile run measures.

Across 16 eligible studies, authors report increased workload, lower work capacity, slower functional-task completion, impaired balance/stability and higher RPE; marksmanship and some physiological effects remain uncertain.
